servers.label: Worktree
servers.summary: Git worktree lifecycle, branch/commit/push plumbing, and repo-wide git queries for parallel ticket work.

tools.name: auth_check_all
tools.description: Check workspace auth token presence for all services (GitHub, Jira, AWS, CI). Returns per-service ok/method/hint. Call at the start of any workflow that requires credentials. Never initiates login flows — read-only token presence check only. If allAuthenticated is false, surface the hint for each failing service and stop; never attempt to generate tokens. Pass `sessionToolNames` to also flag a connector absent from your tool roster (LS-9749).

sessionToolNames.description: Your current tool names, to detect a service whose MCP server is absent from your roster.

tools.name: worktree_attach
tools.description: Attach an existing branch as a new sibling worktree under D:\code\legacy-sports-worktrees\. Use this when resuming work on an existing PR branch — it runs `git worktree add <path> <branch>`, sets the new worktree as active, and optionally runs `make wt-setup`. MCP alternative to raw `git worktree add` via Bash.

branch.description: Existing branch name (e.g. "LS-2857/fix-ci" or "claude/LS-2857-fix-ci"). The branch must already exist locally or on origin.

path.description: Explicit worktree path. Defaults to D:\code\legacy-sports-worktrees\<slug> where slug is derived from the branch name by replacing "/" with "-".

setup.description: If true, run `make wt-setup` after attaching to copy .env, create symlinks, and install git hooks (default: false). Windows-only — ignored on other platforms.

tools.name: worktree_baseline_setup
tools.description: Set up (or tear down) a persistent baseline worktree for an e2e-hold Phase A local comparison against a PR branch: runs `git worktree add`, links node_modules via scripts/modules-pool/link.mjs, and builds the web app (`pnpm exec nx build web`), then returns a ready-to-use worktreePath to pass straight to nx_run_e2e_specs({ worktreePath }). Unlike worktree_run_on_ref (which is one-shot and self-cleaning), the worktree this creates is persistent and keyed by ref — calling it again for the same ref reuses and refreshes it instead of piling up a new checkout. Pass cleanup: true when the comparison is done to remove it.

ref.description: Ref to check out (branch/tag/SHA/remote ref). Default "origin/main".

cleanup.description: If true, remove the baseline worktree for this ref instead of setting one up (default false).

skipBuild.description: Skip the `pnpm exec nx build web` step (default false).

tools.name: worktree_branch
tools.description: Create or switch a local branch within the active worktree's directory — no new worktree/pool slot needed. `action: 'create'` runs `git checkout -b` (off HEAD, or an explicit `from` ref) for a throwaway scratch branch stacked on the active branch, instead of raw git via Bash. `action: 'switch'` runs `git checkout` on an already-existing local branch, e.g. to return to the original branch once a scratch branch is no longer needed. For a brand-new worktree directory on its own branch, use make_worktree_create instead — this tool never creates a new directory.

branch.description: action='create': name of the new branch (e.g. "LS-9411/scratch-mobile-proof"); must not be "main" or "origin/main". action='switch': name of the existing local branch to switch to.

action.description: 'create' to branch and switch; 'switch' to an existing branch.

from.description: action='create' only. Ref (branch, tag, or SHA) to base the new branch on. Omit to base on the worktree's current HEAD.

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree.

tools.name: worktree_check_ignore
tools.description: Check whether paths would be ignored by .gitignore rules (git check-ignore -v). Returns per-path results with the matching rule, source file, and line number. Useful when a newly created file silently disappears from git status.

paths.description: One or more file/directory paths to check (maximum 100). Paths are passed through as provided; only values beginning with `-` are rejected.

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree

tools.name: worktree_checkout_file
tools.description: Restore files to a ref, or resolve conflicts. Alias: paths/path.

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree

tools.name: worktree_clean
tools.description: Remove a worktree safely (symlink-aware). Uses `twig worktree remove` to avoid destroying shared symlinks. Clears active worktree if it was the one removed.

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree

prune.description: Also run `twig worktree clean` to prune stale references (default: true)

force.description: Fall back to `git worktree remove --force` if twig times out or fails. Removes symlinks first to avoid deleting through them. (default: false)

tools.name: worktree_commit
tools.description: Stage and commit. Pass `files` (string or string[]) to stage only specific paths (default: all). Refuses main. Refuses .env/credentials. Supports amend. Pass `resetAuthor: true` with `amend: true` to run `--reset-author` (fixes commit author in cloud sessions). Pass `addAll: true` with `amend: true` (and no `files`) to fold newly-added untracked files into the amended commit (git add -A instead of the default tracked-only git add -u); alternatively pass `files` explicitly for surgical control over exactly which untracked paths to include. Pass `allowEmpty: true` to permit a commit with no staged changes. Auto-appends Co-Authored-By, unless the message already has one or `skipAutoTrailer: true` is passed.

files.description: Files to stage. When provided, ONLY these files are staged (staging area is cleared first). When omitted, new commits stage all changes including untracked files (git add -A), while amend stages only tracked changes (git add -u, after clearing the index) to avoid pulling in untracked files.

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree

worktreeKey.description: Alias for worktree. Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree

worktreeId.description: Alias for worktree. Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree

amend.description: Amend previous commit. If message is provided, replaces the commit message; otherwise uses --no-edit.

resetAuthor.description: When combined with amend: true, passes --reset-author to git commit. Use this in cloud sessions to fix the commit author (git config user.email + --reset-author). Has no effect without amend: true.

addAll.description: When combined with amend: true and no explicit files, stages tracked-modified AND untracked files (git add -A) before amending, instead of the default tracked-only git add -u — use this to fold newly-added files into the amended commit without enumerating every path. Has no effect without amend: true, and is ignored whenever files is provided (files already stages exactly the given paths, tracked or untracked — use it instead of addAll for surgical control). Default: false, preserving today's tracked-only amend behavior.

allowEmpty.description: Pass --allow-empty to git commit, permitting a commit with no staged changes (e.g. an empty files list or a clean tree). Default: false. Use to retrigger CI, unstick a reviewer-bot cycle, or republish a changelog-only commit.

skipAutoTrailer.description: Skip the auto-appended Co-Authored-By trailer. Auto-skipped already when `message` contains a Co-Authored-By:/Claude-Session: line.

tools.name: worktree_commit_batch
tools.description: Commit across multiple worktrees in one call. Each item is processed independently with worktree_commit semantics (refuses main, refuses .env/credentials, auto-appends Co-Authored-By). Failures do not stop remaining items. Returns { total, succeeded, failed } per LS-8033 shared convention.

items.description: Per-worktree commit specs (max 50). Each item accepts the same fields as worktree_commit: worktree (ticket key, path, or branch), message, files, amend, resetAuthor, addAll, skipAutoTrailer.

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or branch name. Required — batch calls cannot fall back to the active worktree.

files.description: Files to stage. Same semantics as worktree_commit.files.

amend.description: Amend previous commit. Same semantics as worktree_commit.amend.

resetAuthor.description: Reset commit author when amending. Same semantics as worktree_commit.resetAuthor.

addAll.description: Fold untracked files into an amended commit (git add -A instead of git add -u). Same semantics as worktree_commit.addAll.

tools.name: worktree_commit_stat
tools.description: Structured JSON stat for a single commit: author, date, subject, per-file insertions/deletions with status (A/M/D/R/C), and totals. Use this instead of `git show <ref> --stat` shell calls when you need a machine-readable file list (e.g. "what files did this commit touch?"). Prefer over worktree_show_commit with stat:true when structured output is needed.

ref.description: Commit SHA, HEAD, HEAD~N, or any git rev (default: HEAD)

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree

tools.name: worktree_conflict_info
tools.description: List conflicted files with line ranges and previews.

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree

tools.name: worktree_delete_remote_branch
tools.description: Delete a remote branch via `git push origin --delete <branch>`. Refuses to delete main or origin/main. Use this to clean up accidentally-pushed branches that have no open PR.

branch.description: Remote branch name to delete (e.g. "claude/LS-1234-my-branch"). Do not include the "origin/" prefix.

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree

tools.name: worktree_diff
tools.description: Git diff against a base ref (default: origin/main). Supports stat/name-only. Pass staged:true to show staged changes (git diff --cached).

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree

base.description: Base ref (default: origin/main). Ignored when staged is true.

paths.description: Path filter — string or string[]. Alias: "files" (either name works; providing both is an error).

files.description: Alias for "paths" — string or string[]. Providing both "paths" and "files" is an error.

staged.description: Show staged changes only (git diff --cached / index vs HEAD). When true, the base ref is ignored.

tools.name: worktree_fetch
tools.description: Fetch from a remote (git fetch [remote] [branch]). Returns real `upToDate`/`ahead`/`behind` (not fetch's stdout) plus shallow state (`isShallow`, `commitCount`) — check before trusting an empty history query as "never existed". Use instead of worktree_run(command: "git fetch origin") before a merge-base check, ancestor comparison, or any op reading origin/* refs — e.g. before worktree_status() for accurate ahead/behind counts. If a merge-base check fails or is empty, the worktree is likely shallow — pass `deepen` or `unshallow: true` (exclusive) instead of raw git via Bash.

branch.description: Specific branch or refspec to fetch (e.g. "main" or "refs/heads/main"). Omit to fetch all branches from the remote.

deepen.description: Deepen a shallow clone by this many commits (`git fetch --deepen=<n>`). Exclusive with `unshallow`.

unshallow.description: Fully unshallow (`git fetch --unshallow`) instead of guessing `deepen`. Exclusive with `deepen`.

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree.

tools.name: worktree_file_info
tools.description: Get metadata for one or more paths (files or directories). Always reports: exists, isFile, isDirectory, isSymlink, isJunction (Windows only), linkTarget (when isSymlink). For regular files ≤10MB also reports bytes, lines, and approxTokens; files >10MB get bytes only. Use this instead of `ls`, `dir`, `Test-Path`, or `Get-ChildItem` to detect whether node_modules is a junction, a real directory, or missing.

paths.description: One or more file paths (max 100). Relative paths are resolved against the worktree root; absolute paths are used as-is.

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree. Used as the root for relative paths.

tools.name: worktree_file_mode
tools.description: Read the git index mode (100644 or 100755) of one or more tracked paths (git ls-files -s). Answers "is this file executable in the index?" without falling back to raw `git ls-files -s` via Bash. Paths not tracked by git are reported with tracked: false rather than erroring.

paths.description: One or more file paths to check (maximum 100). Relative to the worktree root.

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree

tools.name: worktree_guard
tools.description: Check if a path is inside the main repo and warn.

path.description: Path to check

tools.name: worktree_install_recover
tools.description: Recover from a broken pnpm installation in a worktree that has an independent node_modules (not a symlink). Runs the idempotent recovery sequence: (1) kill-stale to release file locks, (2) sweep orphan *_tmp_* directories that block reinstalls, (3) retry pnpm install up to 3 times, removing EPERM/ENOTEMPTY/EBUSY offenders on each failure, (4) if still failing, escalate to pnpm install --force. Returns structured result with attempts made, paths cleaned, and final node_modules state. Do NOT use on symlinked node_modules — run `node scripts/modules-pool/link.mjs` to recreate the symlink instead.

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree.

force.description: Start with pnpm install --force instead of a normal install. Useful when prior recovery attempts have already cleared orphan dirs.

tools.name: worktree_is_tracked
tools.description: Check whether one or more paths are tracked by git (i.e. recorded in the index). Answers the "is this committed source or a build artifact?" question without falling back to `git ls-files <path>` via Bash. Returns tracked/ignored status and file size in one call.

paths.description: One or more file paths to check (maximum 100). Relative to the worktree root.

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree

tools.name: worktree_job_list
tools.description: List recent background jobs (newest first), including jobs started by a previous MCP server process. Use after a session resume or lost tool result to recover a job handle instead of re-running the command.

tools.name: worktree_job_status
tools.description: Cheap, instant snapshot of a background job started by worktree_run or worktree_run_all. Returns { status, elapsedSec, logTail } while running (never an error), or the final output once done. Use worktree_job_wait to block until completion.

jobId.description: Job ID returned by a { status: "running" } result

tools.name: worktree_job_wait
tools.description: Wait for a background job to finish, bounded at 55s per call (stays under the MCP transport timeout). If the job is still running when the wait expires, returns a { status: "running" } snapshot with logTail — re-invoke to continue waiting. Never re-run the underlying command while a job is in progress.

jobId.description: Job ID returned by a { status: "running" } result

maxWaitMs.description: Max wait per call in ms (default and cap: 55000)

tools.name: worktree_list
tools.description: List active worktrees with symlink status and branch info. Pass remote=true to list remote branches instead (with optional pattern or merged-into-ref filters and ahead/behind counts).

remote.description: List remote branches instead of local worktrees (default: false)

pattern.description: Glob pattern to filter results (e.g. "*LS-193*"). Remote: branch names. Local: branch/key/path — plain text substrings, "*"/"?" globs the full value.

merged.description: Only include remote branches merged into this ref (e.g. "origin/main"). Only used when remote=true. Equivalent to `git branch -r --merged <ref>`.

nodeModulesFilter.description: Local only: "stale" = no node_modules (abandoned); "active" = has node_modules.

tools.name: worktree_list_branches
tools.description: List local and/or remote-tracking branches with metadata (type, current-branch marker). Supports substring or regex filtering via the `filter` parameter. Use this to check whether a branch for a given Jira ticket key already exists (e.g. filter: "LS-2955") before creating a new worktree, or to verify no open branches reference a ticket.

filter.description: Substring or JavaScript regex pattern to filter branch names. Examples: "LS-2955" (substring), "^claude/" (regex prefix). Omit to return all branches.

remote.description: Include remote-tracking branches (default: true). Remote branches are listed as "origin/<name>".

tools.name: worktree_lock
tools.description: Acquire an advisory lock on a worktree for multi-agent coordination. Signals to other agents that the worktree is in use so they should avoid modifying it concurrently. Locks have a TTL and are automatically cleaned up when stale.

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree

agent.description: Agent identifier (e.g. session ID, agent name). Defaults to "claude-session".

task.description: Human-readable description of what the agent is doing (optional).

ttl.description: Lock TTL in seconds (default: 7200 = 2 hours). Lock expires after this period.

force.description: Force-acquire even if another agent holds the lock (default: false).

tools.name: worktree_log
tools.description: Structured commit log as JSON.

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree

path.description: File path filter

since.description: Only show commits more recent than this date. Accepts any format `git log --since` accepts (e.g. "2026-04-03 15:00", "2.weeks.ago", ISO 8601). Combine with `until` to bracket a window.

until.description: Only show commits older than this date. Accepts any format `git log --until` accepts. Combine with `since` to bracket a window.

searchString.description: Pickaxe search (`git log -S`). Only show commits whose diff adds or removes the literal string. Combine with `path` to scope to a single file. Example: searchString="playwright_version" answers "when did this constant first appear?".

searchRegex.description: Generalized pickaxe (`git log -G`). Like `searchString` but the value is treated as a regular expression. Mutually compatible with `searchString` (both forwarded to git, but typically use one at a time).

file.description: Restrict log to commits that touched this file path (maps to `git log -- <file>`). Alias for `path` — use either; `file` takes precedence when both are provided. Example: file="apps/web/src/pages/Login.tsx" answers "which commits last modified this file?".

grep.description: Filter commits whose message matches this pattern (maps to `git log --grep=<pattern>`). Useful for finding commits by Jira ticket key, e.g. grep="LS-2433". The pattern is matched case-insensitively against the full commit message.

stat.description: Include per-commit file change stats. Each entry in the `files` array has `path`, `status` (A=added, M=modified, D=deleted, R=renamed, C=copied), `insertions`, and `deletions`. Use maxCount=1 + stat=true as a replacement for `git show --stat HEAD` or `git diff HEAD~1 HEAD --name-status`.

tools.name: worktree_ls_tree
tools.description: List files at a git ref without checkout (git ls-tree).

ref.description: Git ref to list from (default: "HEAD"). Accepts any rev: branch, tag, or SHA.

path.description: Directory path (relative to root)

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree

tools.name: worktree_merge_main
tools.description: Semantic one-shot merge: fetch origin/main → merge it into the current branch → push. Complements worktree_rebase_onto_main for the merge-resolution path AGENTS.md sanctions for PR merge-conflict notices ("merge the base branch ... into your PR head — or rebase"). On conflict, leaves the merge in progress (does not abort) and returns the same structured conflict info worktree_conflict_info provides (conflicted file list + marker locations) — resolve, then worktree_commit + worktree_push, or worktree_run(command: "git merge --abort") to back out. Refuses to operate on the main branch. `dryRun: true` — see that param.

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree.

pushTimeoutMs.description: Timeout for git push in milliseconds (default: 120000).

dryRun.description: No mutation: report mergeable/conflicted + conflicting files (default: false).

tools.name: worktree_mv
tools.description: Move or rename one or more tracked files (git mv), preserving rename detection so the diff shows R instead of a delete+add pair. Creates intermediate directories in the destination path since git mv does not. Refuses paths outside the worktree root, .git/, or node_modules/. Accepts multiple { from, to } pairs in one call for batch moves (e.g. moving a source file and its spec together).

moves.description: One or more { from, to } path pairs to move/rename (maximum 50 per call).

from.description: Current path, relative to the worktree root.

to.description: New path, relative to the worktree root.

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree.

tools.name: worktree_ping
tools.description: Check connectivity and state of the worktree server. Returns git version, main repo path, active worktree, and total worktree count. Use this to verify the server is running correctly before using other worktree_* tools.

tools.name: worktree_push
tools.description: Push with --force-with-lease. Refuses main.

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree

worktreeKey.description: Alias for worktree. Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree

worktreeId.description: Alias for worktree. Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree

setUpstream.description: Set upstream (-u). Also accepts string "true"/"false"/"1"/"0" (MCP framework coercion).

skipLint.description: Set SKIP_PREPUSH_LINT=1 before pushing. Use when pnpm virtual store is absent and the pre-push formatter hook fails. Also accepts string "true"/"false"/"1"/"0" (MCP framework coercion).

remoteBranch.description: Push to this remote branch name instead of the local branch name. Must contain an LS-#### Jira key; pushes are refused otherwise. Providing remoteBranch also implies upstream is set (-u). ⚠️ Do NOT use this in native ephemeral (launcher-checkbox) sessions — local/remote name mismatch confuses PR association in the Claude Code UI (anthropics/claude-code#18690). Jira linking for native ephemeral sessions is done via PR title and commit messages containing LS-####, not the branch name. See .agents/skills/worktree-workflow/references/branch-naming.md.

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds for the git push subprocess (default: 120000). Increase when pre-push hooks run slow checks (e.g. terraform validate, pnpm format) that exceed the default.

tools.name: worktree_push_batch
tools.description: Push multiple worktrees in one call with --force-with-lease. Each item is processed independently with worktree_push semantics (refuses main). Failures do not stop remaining items. Returns { total, succeeded, failed } per LS-8033 shared convention.

items.description: Per-worktree push specs (max 50). Each item accepts the same fields as worktree_push: worktree (required), setUpstream, skipLint, remoteBranch, timeoutMs, fetchFirst.

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or branch name. Required — batch calls cannot fall back to the active worktree.

tools.name: worktree_read
tools.description: Read the contents of any file on the local filesystem by absolute path. Use this for files outside the project directory (e.g. /tmp, ~/Downloads, C:\\Users\\...). For files inside the project directory, the built-in Read tool is preferred. Supports optional line ranges (startLine/endLine) and grep filtering.

path.description: Absolute path to the file to read (e.g. "/tmp/extracted/design.md" or "C:\\Users\\user\\Downloads\\handoff.txt").

startLine.description: First line to return (1-based, inclusive). Omit to return the full file.

endLine.description: Last line to return (1-based, inclusive). Requires startLine.

grep.description: Optional JavaScript RegExp source string. When provided, only matching lines (with line numbers) are returned. Mutually exclusive with startLine/endLine.

maxMatches.description: Max number of matched lines to return when `grep` is provided (default: 50, max: 500).

tools.name: worktree_rebase
tools.description: Fetch and rebase onto parent. Accepts an optional 'base' parameter to rebase onto an explicit branch (e.g. 'origin/main') when the branch has no twig parent registered. Run worktree_stabilize after rebasing, before pushing.

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree

base.description: Explicit git ref or commit-ish to rebase onto, e.g. 'origin/main' or 'HEAD~3'. Defaults to twig parent if omitted; falls back to 'origin/main' if twig has no parent registered. Cannot be combined with 'abort' or 'skip'.

disableRerere.description: Disable rerere (reuse recorded resolution) for this rebase. Pass true when a bad rr-cache entry is causing conflict markers to be silently committed.

tools.name: worktree_rebase_continue
tools.description: Continue rebase after resolving conflicts.

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree

tools.name: worktree_rebase_onto_main
tools.description: Semantic one-shot rebase: fetch origin/main → rebase current branch onto it → push with --force-with-lease. Replaces the three-step worktree_fetch → worktree_rebase(base: "origin/main") → worktree_push sequence. Pass `upstream` for the `--onto` 3-arg form after a squash-merged stacked base (see worktree-workflow skill). Aborts and reports if conflict markers are detected post-rebase rather than pushing a broken state. Refuses to operate on the main branch.

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree.

upstream.description: Old base head to replay from — enables `git rebase --onto <onto> <upstream>`. Omit for a plain rebase onto `onto`; see worktree-workflow skill for when to set this.

disableRerere.description: Disable git rerere during the rebase (set rerere.enabled=false). Use when a bad rr-cache entry is causing silent conflict-marker commits.

pushTimeoutMs.description: Timeout for git push in milliseconds (default: 120000).

tools.name: worktree_reflog
tools.description: Show the reflog for a worktree — all HEAD movements including commits removed by reset --hard, amend, and rebase. Use this to recover SHAs after destructive operations (reset --hard, bad rebase, accidental amend). Prefer this over `git reflog` shell calls. Substitutes: `git reflog` → `worktree_reflog()`, `git reflog | head -20` → `worktree_reflog({ limit: 20 })`.

limit.description: Max reflog entries to return (default: 20, max: 100)

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree

tools.name: worktree_remove_batch
tools.description: Remove multiple worktrees in one call using `twig worktree remove`. Symlink-aware — safer than `git worktree remove`. Use for bulk sweep pruning. Each worktree entry is processed independently; failures do not stop remaining removals.

worktrees.description: Worktrees to remove. Each entry can be a ticket key (e.g. "LS-1234"), branch name (e.g. "LS-1234/foo"), directory name, or absolute path. Maximum 100.

force.description: Fall back to `git worktree remove --force` (with symlink removal first) when twig fails. Default: false.

tools.name: worktree_rename_branch
tools.description: Rename the current branch in the active (or specified) worktree. Use this after `jira_create_ticket` returns the LS key to rename the auto-generated `claude/<random>` branch to `claude/LS-####-description` before the first push (AGENTS.md Step 4b). MCP alternative to `git branch -m <newName>` via Bash.

newName.description: New branch name. Must contain an LS-#### Jira key (e.g. "claude/LS-2994-add-rename-tool"). Must not be "main" or "origin/main".

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree.

tools.name: worktree_rename_session
tools.description: Set the display title for the current Claude Code session. Appends a custom-title entry to the session JSONL so the session appears with the given title in /resume and the session list. Call after jira_view to set the title to "LS-#### <ticket summary>". Safe to call multiple times — the last title wins.

title.description: New session title (e.g. "LS-3052 feat(skills): add session rename"). Must be non-empty.

worktree.description: Ticket key or absolute path whose session to rename. Omit to use the active worktree (or main repo if none active).

tools.name: worktree_rerere_forget
tools.description: Clear the cached rerere resolution for one or more files, for recovery when rerere has stored a bad resolution during a rebase/merge conflict. If a file no longer has conflict markers (rerere already auto-applied its resolution), it is reset to the conflicted state first (`git checkout --merge`) before forgetting — this is the default, unconditional behavior, since it is the only safe way to clear rerere for an already-resolved file. Never throws on partial failure; returns { cleared, failed } per-file so recovery can continue with manual conflict resolution.

paths.description: File path(s) to clear the rerere cache for.

worktree.description: Ticket key, absolute path, or omit for active worktree

tools.name: worktree_reset
tools.description: Reset HEAD to a specific commit SHA (git reset). Safety: refuses main branch and only allows resetting to ancestor SHAs (commits reachable from HEAD) to prevent accidental data loss. Typical use: strip a stray commit and restore the branch before force-pushing with worktree_push.

sha.description: Target commit SHA to reset to.

mode.description: Reset mode (default: 'hard'). 'hard' resets index and working tree. 'soft' moves HEAD only, leaving changes staged. 'mixed' resets index but leaves working tree unchanged.

force.description: Skip the dirty-worktree check for --hard resets. Default false (refuses if uncommitted changes exist); true discards them.

allowNonAncestor.description: Default false. If true, allow non-ancestor sha in reflog.

tools.name: ci_run_custom_checks

Each script is a cheap, self-contained `node --test` runner with no external deps. Prefer this over raw `bash .github/checks/<name>.sh` or `node --test <path>` via shell — it discovers every script automatically and reports pass/fail per script in one call, instead of stopping at the first failure the way the CI step does. Running the relevant check before pushing catches failures (e.g. a missing e2e-surface-map.json entry) that would otherwise cost a CI round-trip. Pass `scripts` to run a named subset (e.g. ["integration-select-tests"] — the .sh suffix is optional); omit it to run every discovered script. Defaults to `verbosity: "failures"` to keep full runs small.

A target still running after ~45s returns { status: "running", jobId }; call make_run_wait({ jobId }) to keep waiting and do NOT re-run it. The pc pipeline also runs as ordered chunks (pc-db-prep, pc-typecheck, pc-lint, pc-format, pc-workflows, pc-test, pc-build) — equivalent to `pc` only when all run in that order. runner-apply prompts interactively: always pass variables="NO_CONFIRM=1". Target details and per-environment validation: .agents/skills/repo-tooling/SKILL.md.

Returns { migrations: { applied, pending, needsMigration }, pc: { passed, steps, errors } }. The default runs make pc as a background job with a ~45s bounded wait: if pc is still running the result is { pc: { status: "running", jobId } } — poll with make_run_wait({ jobId }), never re-invoke while it runs. runPcInBackground: true skips the bounded wait and returns the jobId immediately. Use sanctionedChunks: true to run the seven pc steps individually (pc-db-prep → pc-typecheck → pc-lint → pc-format → pc-workflows → pc-test → pc-build); each call is budgeted to ~45s and may return { pc: { status: "in_progress", ... } } with resume instructions (re-invoke with startAtChunk, or make_run_wait a still-running chunk job) — never restart validation from scratch.

Fast installs return in one call; a slow one returns { status: "running", jobId } — poll nx_job_wait({ jobId }), do NOT re-run.

tools.name: nx_job_list
tools.description: List recent background jobs (newest first), including jobs started by a previous MCP server process. Use after a session resume or lost tool result to recover a job handle instead of re-running validation.

tools.name: nx_job_status
tools.description: Cheap, instant snapshot of a background job started by a job-backed nx tool (nx_run_pc_chunk, nx_run, nx_run_affected, nx_run_e2e_specs, nx_install_package). Returns { status, elapsedSec, logTail } while running (never an error), or the final pass/fail output once done. Use nx_job_wait to block until completion.

jobId.description: Job ID returned by a { status: "running" } result

tools.name: nx_job_wait
tools.description: Wait for a background job to finish, bounded at 55s per call (stays under the MCP transport timeout). If the job is still running when the wait expires, returns a { status: "running" } snapshot with logTail — re-invoke to continue waiting. Never re-run the underlying command while a job is in progress.

jobId.description: Job ID returned by a { status: "running" } result

maxWaitMs.description: Max wait per call in ms (default and cap: 55000)

tools.name: nx_run
tools.description: Prefer this over `pnpm exec nx run <project>:<target>` / `pnpm exec nx run-many -t <target>` via shell. Runs an Nx target on one project, or fans out across every project declaring it if `project` is omitted. Allowed: build, test, lint, typecheck, codegen, serve, dev, print-schema, deploy:plan, e2e, integration, storybook, format (colon-suffixed variants accepted). Fast targets return pass/fail in one call; a slow run returns { status: "running", jobId } after ~45s — call nx_job_wait({ jobId }); do NOT re-run.

project.description: Project name. Omit or pass "all" to fan out across every project declaring the target.

updateSnapshot.description: Update Jest snapshots (appends --updateSnapshot). Only applies to the "test" target.

args.description: Extra flags after "--" (e.g. ["--verbose"] for verbose output). Array preferred; string split on whitespace. For multiple test patterns, pipe is preferred: ["--testPathPatterns", "FileA|FileB"]. Separate array elements also work: ["--testPathPatterns", "FileA", "FileB"] — on Windows these are automatically coalesced into a single pipe-separated token.

env.description: Environment variables to set for the command (e.g. { "PLAYWRIGHT_GREP": "@regression" }).

tools.name: nx_run_affected
tools.description: Prefer this over `pnpm exec nx affected -t <target>` via shell. Run an Nx target on all affected projects. Allowed: build, test, lint, typecheck, codegen. A run still going after ~45s returns { status: "running", jobId } — call nx_job_wait({ jobId }) to continue waiting; do NOT re-run (re-invoking joins the in-flight run).

target.description: Target to run on affected projects

tools.name: nx_run_e2e_specs
tools.description: Prefer this over raw `npx playwright test` shell commands. Hermetic mode (default): runs specs from src/tests/ against a local static build, auto-selects a free E2E_PORT, and forces E2E_AUTH_MODE=ci (no OAuth needed). Requires dist/apps/web — run nx_run({ project: "web", target: "build" }) first if missing. Integration mode (integration: true): runs specs from src/integration/tests/ against the live backend (api.legacy-fantasy.com) with workers=1 to avoid throttling. Checks e2e JWT freshness (~/.legacy-sports/e2e-token.json) and E2EPOOLPASSWORD before launching. Set withTracing: true to enable Playwright tracing in either mode; trace.zip paths are returned in traceArtifacts. Returns a compact summary: pass/fail counts, failing test details, raw output, traceArtifacts, and (integration only) graphqlErrors. A run still going after ~45s returns { status: "running", jobId } — call nx_job_wait({ jobId }) for the same structured summary once done; do NOT re-run (re-invoking joins the in-flight run). The underlying Playwright process is hard-killed after 30 minutes (hermetic) / 8 minutes (integration) independent of how many nx_job_wait calls you make — large hermetic batches (100+ specs) usually finish well within that, but if you hit the kill, split specs into smaller batches across multiple calls.

specs.description: Spec file paths relative to apps/web-e2e/ (e.g. ["src/tests/roster-management.spec.ts"] for hermetic, "src/integration/tests/league.spec.ts" for integration). Absolute paths are also accepted.

project.description: Playwright project/browser to run against. Allowed: chromium, firefox, webkit, Mobile Chrome, Mobile Safari (default: chromium).

grep.description: Filter tests by title regex (Playwright --grep). E.g. "@critical" or "should show roster".

integration.description: When true, runs specs against the live backend using playwright.integration.config.ts instead of the hermetic config. Enforces workers=1. Checks JWT freshness and E2EPOOLPASSWORD before launching.

withTracing.description: When true, enables Playwright tracing (--trace=on) in either mode. Trace zip paths are returned in traceArtifacts.

skipGlobalSetup.description: Integration mode only. Skips globalSetup and the JWT/E2EPOOLPASSWORD preflight, for hermetic *.contract.spec.ts files.

tools.name: nx_run_eslint
tools.description: Prefer this over raw `pnpm exec eslint <files>` via shell when you need to lint a small, explicit file list. Runs eslint against exactly the given files, and from the nearest directory owning an eslint.config.* so the project's flat config actually applies (ESLint 9 resolves flat config from its cwd, not per file). A file list spanning two config roots is rejected — split it into one call per root. Capped at ${ESLINT_MAX_FILES} files. Verdict agrees with pc-lint by default: errors fail, warnings alone don't; pass maxWarnings to opt into a stricter threshold. Result has errorCount/warningCount fields. IMPORTANT — NOT a fast path here: type-aware rules force a full TypeScript program build per run (~280s in lambdas/db), regardless of file count. Use for a narrow report; use nx_run({ project, target: "lint" }) for a whole (cached) project, nx_run_pc_chunk({ chunk: "pc-lint" }) for the repo. A run still going after ~45s returns { status: "running", jobId } — call nx_job_wait to continue; do NOT re-run.

files.description: Paths to lint: relative to `project` root if given (falling back to repo-root), else repo-root/worktreePath-relative or absolute. Must share one eslint.config.* root.

project.description: Nx project name to resolve `files` against.

maxWarnings.description: eslint --max-warnings. Omit for unlimited (matches pc-lint: only errors fail); pass 0 for strict.

tools.name: nx_run_pc_chunk
tools.description: Prefer this over `make pc-<chunk>` via shell for cloud agents. Run a single pre-commit validation chunk. Chunks must run IN ORDER: pc-db-prep → pc-typecheck → pc-lint → pc-format → pc-workflows → pc-test → pc-build. Fast chunks return structured pass/fail output in one call. A chunk still running after ~45s returns { status: "running", jobId } instead of blocking into the ~60s MCP transport timeout — the chunk keeps running in the background; call nx_job_wait({ jobId }) to continue waiting. Do NOT re-run the chunk: re-invoking while it runs joins the in-flight job.

chunk.description: Pre-commit validation chunk to run. One of: ${PC_CHUNKS.join(', ')}

verbose.description: When true, include the full raw output (up to 30k chars) in the response instead of the default compact summary. Default false: prettier per-file listings (pc-format) are collapsed to a count, and the step body (e.g. eslint output for pc-lint) is truncated to 20 lines with a note to run the step directly for the rest. Use verbose: true only when you need the complete output for debugging.

maxWorkers.description: Cap Jest worker parallelism for the pc-test chunk by passing MAXWORKERS=<n>, which the pc-test recipe forwards to `nx affected -t test` as `-- --maxWorkers=<n>`. Use on memory-constrained machines to avoid "Fatal process out of memory: Zone" crashes (with "spawn UNKNOWN" in jest-worker) from full-parallelism Jest workers across every affected project — that failure signature means retry pc-test with a lower maxWorkers, not that the code under test regressed. E.g. maxWorkers: 2. Ignored by chunks other than pc-test.

parallel.description: Cap nx project-level parallelism for the pc-lint chunk by passing PARALLEL=<n>, which the pc-lint recipe forwards to `nx affected -t lint --fix` as `--parallel=<n>` (nx.json default: 5). Use on memory-constrained machines to avoid individual large projects (e.g. lambdas/db, cli) getting "Killed" (OOM) when several `eslint . --fix` processes run concurrently, each ballooning to 2-5GB RSS — nx may then mislabel the OOM-killed project "flaky" on retry, masking the real cause. E.g. parallel: 2. Ignored by chunks other than pc-lint.

tools.name: nx_run_prettier
tools.description: Prefer this over raw `pnpm exec prettier --check/--write <files>` via shell, and over nx_run_pc_chunk({ chunk: "pc-format" }) when you only need a small, explicit file list (e.g. fixing Prettier drift in 1-3 files after a rebase). Runs prettier --check or --write against exactly the given files — never the whole repo diff — so it carries none of pc-format's auto-amend-already-pushed-commit risk (LS-8367) or full per-file-listing overflow risk (LS-8423). Capped at ${PRETTIER_MAX_FILES} files — for broader formatting use nx_run_pc_chunk({ chunk: "pc-format" }) instead. Works on any file in the repo, including files outside every Nx project (e.g. top-level scripts/, like scripts/modules-pool/link.mjs) — there is no Nx project resolution here at all, just prettier run directly against the given paths.

files.description: File paths (relative to worktreePath/repo root, or absolute) to check or format.

mode.description: "check" reports formatting issues without modifying files (default); "write" reformats in place.

tools.name: nx_run_test
tools.description: Prefer this over raw `npx jest --config <path> --testPathPatterns <pattern> -t <name>` via shell when narrowing to one spec/test. Wrapper over nx_run: resolves `config` to the matching jest target (e.g. "mobile" -> "test:mobile") and forwards testPathPatterns/testNamePattern. Omit `config` for a single "test" target (fans out for aggregate targets, e.g. shared-components; auto-routes to `files` for a `node --test` target, e.g. ci-reviewer). Same job semantics as nx_run — call nx_job_wait if slow. On a failing run pass report: "summary" for the full failing-test list; the raw log is truncated and cuts through the middle of it.

testPathPatterns.description: Jest --testPathPatterns value: a spec filename or regex pattern (e.g. "LeagueListRow"). For multiple patterns, pipe-separate: "FileA|FileB". Capped at 300 characters and rejects nested-quantifier shapes like "(a+)+" (ReDoS) — use a simple spec name/pattern. Required unless the target runs `node --test`, where `files` is used instead.

files.description: Project-relative file paths, for a "test" target running `node --test` instead of Jest (e.g. ["lib/__tests__/retry.test.mjs"]). Unused for Jest targets.

testNamePattern.description: Jest -t value: filters to matching test names, e.g. "DraftSquadStrip". Same length cap and ReDoS guard as testPathPatterns.

config.description: Jest config variant, mapped to the "test:<config>" target (e.g. "mobile", "web", "stories"). Omit for projects with a single "test" target.

report.description: Structured failures parsed from jest --json. "summary": counts plus failures: [{ suite, fullName, message }], ANSI-stripped, each message clipped to ~10 lines, no raw log. "json": adds the raw output. Omit for the default shape. Pair with noCache: true — an Nx cache replay writes no report.

tools.name: nx_show_project
tools.description: Inspect a project: root, targets, tags, type.

tools.name: nx_show_projects
tools.description: List Nx projects. Filter by affected, target, or tag.

withTarget.description: Filter to projects with this target

servers.label: CI
servers.summary: GitHub Actions run triage: list/view runs, fetch and search logs, rerun failed jobs, and read Playwright reports.

tools.name: ci_audit_session_bash
tools.description: Extract Bash tool_use calls (and optionally MCP overflows/failures) from the current Claude Code session transcript, including subagent transcripts, so the inventory survives context compaction. Auto-detects the current session and project, worktree sessions included. Output modes: default structured JSON; gapsOnly for a compact frequency table; auditMode for a pre-classified gap report with confidence scores and draft ticket summaries. Drives the MCP gap audit — see .agents/skills/mcp-first/references/audit-workflow.md.

sessionId.description: Session UUID. Defaults to the most recently modified JSONL in the project directory.

project.description: Project slug (e.g. "D--code-legacy-sports"). Auto-detected from CWD if omitted.

projectsDir.description: Base directory holding project session folders. Overrides auto-detection; cannot help in CCR — use `make audit-session` (LS-8890).

transcriptContent.description: Raw transcript JSONL; bypasses path resolution (no shared filesystem case, LS-9362).

includeMcp.description: Include MCP tool overflows and failures in the report (default: false).

pid.description: Process ID to look up session ID from ~/.claude/sessions/.

gapsOnly.description: Compact output: one line per unique command pattern (<5 KB), gaps separated from covered commands.

scanScratch.description: Also scan scratch/*.py for subprocess shell patterns; reported under "scratch_subprocess_calls".

auditMode.description: Full audit report: pre-classified gaps with confidence scores, draft ticket summaries, noise filtering, and overflow/failure triage. Implies includeMcp. Review and approve rather than classify from scratch.

sessionToolNames.description: Your current tool names — reclassifies `gh pr *`/`gh run *` as a real gap when the covering MCP server is absent from this list, instead of always "covered" (LS-9749).

tools.name: ci_auth_status
tools.description: Check if the CI server is authenticated with GitHub. Returns token source (GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, github-app, or gh-cli), authenticated user login, and rate limit info for whichever token that source resolved to. Call this first to verify credentials are working before using other ci_* tools. Also see github_auth_status for basic GitHub auth status without rate limit info. NOTE: rateLimit here is not guaranteed to be the installation bucket (GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN take precedence when set) — use ci_installation_rate_limit for that specifically.

tools.name: ci_auto_fix
tools.description: Classify a CI failure into a category (formatting, stale_branch, codegen, type_error, test_failure, lint, flaky, infrastructure, unknown) with confidence, evidence, and fix recommendation.

tools.name: ci_cancel_run
tools.description: Prefer this over `gh run cancel` via shell. Cancel a single in-flight run via runId — e.g. killing a stale-SHA dispatch after pushing a follow-up commit — or every in-flight (queued/in_progress) run of a workflow on a branch via workflow+branch (e.g. serializing expensive live-backend integration runs so a fresh dispatch never races a stale one, LS-7878); pass one mode, not both. Single-run mode re-fetches the run after cancelling since GitHub does not transition synchronously (it passes through `cancel_in_progress` first); cancelling an already-completed run returns a clear error rather than throwing. Bulk mode resolves `workflow` the same way ci_list_runs does and returns the standard partial-failure shape { success, total, succeeded, failed }, with total: 0 when nothing is in flight.

runId.description: Run ID to cancel (single-run mode). Use the "id" field from ci_list_runs output ("databaseId" is an alias).

workflow.description: Workflow filename, display name, or numeric ID (bulk mode, with branch).

branch.description: Branch to scope bulk cancellation to (bulk mode, with workflow).

tools.name: ci_deploys_repo_auth_status
tools.description: Diagnose why ci_get_playwright_report/ci_get_playwright_test_result might 404 on the private bkrupa/legacy-sports-deploys repo (LS-8788) — WITHOUT triggering a real report fetch. Explicitly exercises each credential tier getDeploysToken() tries, in order: (1) PREVIEW_APP_PRIVATE_KEY + PREVIEW_APP_ID (dedicated deploy App), (2) the agent-author App's own installation on the deploys repo. Reports which tier is configured, which succeeded/failed and why, and which source `resolvedSource` a real ci_get_playwright_report call would actually use right now. `resolvedSource: "fallback"` means both tiers are unavailable and reads will 404 with the "broad fallback token" credentials-gap message — see .agents/skills/read-playwright-report/SKILL.md for the two known remedies (both require one-time human action outside this repo). Call this to verify a credentials fix actually landed instead of re-triggering a report fetch and re-deriving the same diagnosis from a 404.

tools.name: ci_dispatch_workflow
tools.description: Trigger a GitHub Actions workflow_dispatch event. Accepts a workflow file name (e.g. "deploy.yml"), numeric ID, or display name (e.g. "Legacy Sports CI Orchestrator") — resolved the same way as ci_list_runs, plus optional ref and input parameters. Set waitForCompletion: true to wait for the run (bounded at ~20s per call to stay under this Lambda-hosted server's own 30s execution timeout): fast runs return the final conclusion in one call; longer runs return { status: "in_progress", runId } — continue with ci_wait_run({ runId }), never by re-dispatching. This is the MCP-native alternative to `gh run watch` for non-PR dispatched runs — avoids the shell fallback and session-resume watcher-death problem. When waitForCompletion is false (default), the tool returns immediately and the agent must use ci_list_runs then ci_view_run to track the run. Note: PR-associated runs notify natively via push events; use waitForCompletion only for workflow_dispatch runs that have no associated PR.

inputs.description: Key-value map of workflow input parameters (all values must be strings). Accepts either a plain object or a JSON string.

waitForCompletion.description: When true, polls the triggered run for up to ~20s and returns { status: "completed", conclusion, ... } if it finishes, or { status: "in_progress", runId, hint } if not — continue waiting with ci_wait_run({ runId }). Use this instead of `gh run watch` for non-PR workflow_dispatch runs. Default: false.

timeoutSeconds.description: Deprecated — the per-call wait is always clamped to ~20s (this Lambda-hosted server's own execution timeout, not the MCP transport deadline). Kept for backward compatibility; longer waits are re-armed via ci_wait_run.

tools.name: ci_download_artifact
tools.description: Prefer this over `gh run download` via shell. Download a named GitHub Actions artifact from a workflow run. Without outDir, file contents return inline (UTF-8 or base64, ~200KB cap — the only option in hosted sessions). With outDir, files are extracted there and only paths returned.

runId.description: Workflow run ID that produced the artifact

artifactName.description: Exact artifact name (falls back to a case-insensitive match)

outDir.description: Local directory to extract into. Omit for inline contents.

tools.name: ci_find_session
tools.description: Find Claude Code session JSONL files containing a substring (e.g. a Jira key, branch name, or commit SHA). Scans every JSONL under ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/ — including subagent transcripts — and returns matches sorted by last-modified descending. Use this to locate "where did I work on LS-#### earlier today?" without manually grepping session files. Empty matches array if nothing found.

query.description: Substring to search for in session JSONLs (e.g. "LS-2366", "fix-nightly-playwright", a git SHA).

project.description: Project slug (e.g. "D--code-legacy-sports"). Auto-detected from CWD if omitted.

includeSubagents.description: Also scan subagent JSONLs under <sessionId>/subagents/ (default: true).

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 50, max: 500). Older matches are dropped first.

tools.name: ci_force_cancel_run
tools.description: Last resort for a run ci_cancel_run cannot actually evict — e.g. a job queued for a self-hosted runner that has already shut down, so GitHub has no runner left to deliver a graceful cancel signal to (LS-9709). Calls GitHub's POST .../force-cancel endpoint, which GitHub itself documents as a more disruptive last resort, so this refuses to run unless confirmNormalCancelFailed is explicitly true — always try ci_cancel_run({ runId }) first. Unlike a bare API call, this does not trust "request accepted" on its own: it polls the run afterward until it actually reaches a terminal state (or the poll budget runs out) and reports which — { status: "terminated" } only when the run is confirmed completed with conclusion "cancelled", { status: "cancelling", hint } if still not terminal (re-invoke to keep polling), or { status: "already-completed" } / { status: "completed-otherwise" } when there was nothing to force.

runId.description: Run ID to force-cancel. Use the "id" field from ci_list_runs output ("databaseId" is an alias).

confirmNormalCancelFailed.description: Must be true to proceed. Set this only after ci_cancel_run({ runId }) has already been called for this run and the run is still not terminating.

maxWaitSeconds.description: How long to poll for confirmed termination after force-cancelling (default/cap: 20s, this Lambda's own execution budget). If the run is still not terminal when the budget runs out, re-invoke with the same runId and confirmNormalCancelFailed: true to keep polling.

tools.name: ci_get_logs
tools.description: Prefer this over `gh run view --log-failed` via shell. Fetch CI logs for a run or job, failed steps only by default. Response is a minified-JSON metadata line followed by raw log text.

runId.description: Run ID (required when jobId and runIds are not provided)

runIds.description: Batch mode: up to 10 runs, each a "=== run <id> ===" section; runs with expired logs go to missing[]. Not with jobId.

jobName.description: Job name — exact match, else substring; errors if ambiguous.

maxLines.description: Max lines returned (cap 5000). Default 500, or up to 10000 when errorSummary is set.

maxChars.description: Hard cap on total characters (default 50000), applied regardless of maxLines.

truncateLineLength.description: Truncate individual lines past this length.

errorSummary.description: Extract only error/failure lines with context (~200 lines max).

offset.description: Skip this many lines before applying maxChars, to page a log across calls; response meta gives the next offset.

grep.description: Regex filter over the full log, e.g. "foo|bar". Overrides errorSummary. Capped at 300 matches.

tools.name: ci_get_playwright_report
tools.description: Read a Playwright E2E test report deployed to legacy-sports-deploys. Returns overall stats (total/passed/failed/skipped/flaky), per-file breakdowns, lists of failed/flaky test titles, and a skippedTests array with { name, file, reason } for every skipped test (reason comes from the test annotation description). Pass prNumber to auto-resolve the report for a PR (e.g. { prNumber: 5271 }). Pass runId to auto-resolve by GitHub Actions run ID (auto-expanded to nightly-/manual- fallbacks). Pass reportName when you already know the exact deployed name (e.g. "pr-2173", "manual-146"). At least one of prNumber, runId, or reportName is required. If multiple are provided, prNumber takes precedence, then runId, then reportName. Examples: ci_get_playwright_report({ prNumber: 5271 }) · ci_get_playwright_report({ runId: 12345678 }) · ci_get_playwright_report({ reportName: "pr-2173" })

reportName.description: Exact report name as deployed: "pr-{number}" for PRs (e.g. "pr-2173"), "manual-{number}" for manually-triggered runs (e.g. "manual-146"), "nightly-{run_id}" for nightly runs, or a bare numeric GitHub run ID (auto-expanded to nightly-/manual- fallbacks). Omit when using prNumber or runId.

prNumber.description: GitHub PR number. Auto-resolves to the report deployed under "pr-{prNumber}". Use this when triaging CI failures on a specific PR.

runId.description: GitHub Actions workflow run ID. Auto-expanded to nightly-{id} or manual-{id} fallbacks when not found directly.

tools.name: ci_get_playwright_test_result
tools.description: Read a SINGLE test result from a Playwright report, or list S3 blob artifacts for a CI run. Prefer this over ci_get_playwright_report when you already know which test failed and want only its error, snippet, stdout/stderr, and attachments — it keeps the full report out of context. Identify the report with reportName or runId, and the test with testTitle and/or fileName/testFile; an ambiguous match returns a candidates list. Report naming, S3 blob handling, and the runId+testFile webhook lookup: .agents/skills/read-playwright-report/SKILL.md.

reportName.description: Deployed report name (pr-N, manual-N, nightly-<runId>) or a bare numeric run ID. Alternative to runId; one is required.

runId.description: GitHub Actions run ID (e.g. from the <integration-results> webhook). Alternative to reportName; one is required.

testTitle.description: Case-insensitive substring of the full title (describe path joined by " > "). Optional when fileName/testFile is given.

fileName.description: Case-insensitive spec-filename substring, to disambiguate identical titles (gh-pages mode). Alias: testFile.

testFile.description: Alias for fileName, matching the <integration-results> webhook field. One of testTitle or fileName/testFile is required.

source.description: "gh-pages" (default) or "s3" (presigned blob-archive URLs) — use s3 when the GH Pages report is absent.

artifactType.description: s3 mode only: artifact prefix. Default "blobs".

maxChars.description: Reserved for future use. gh-pages mode applies a fixed 4000-char per-field cap; s3 presigned URLs are never truncated.

tools.name: ci_installation_rate_limit
tools.description: Report the Agent Author App installation token's core rate limit. NOT the budget of workflow steps using github.token/secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN (separate per-repo budget, unreadable here) or other Apps — healthy here does not mean CI is not rate limited (LS-10491). After a CI rate-limit 403 or withheld status, pass its runId/jobId: the tool scans the logs for rate-limit 403s and App-token mint failures and returns a verdict on which bucket was hit. Never re-run immediately.

tools.name: ci_is_head_sha
tools.description: Prefer this over a manual pull_request_read + ci_list_runs/ci_view_run cross-check when a webhook-delivered check-run or CI-comment event needs to be checked for staleness. Answers, in one cheap call, whether the given sha is still the PR's current head — replacing the two-call manual cross-check previously needed to tell whether an event refers to a since-superseded commit (LS-9267).

prNumber.description: PR number to check the current head SHA of.

sha.description: The commit SHA from the webhook event (check-run head_sha, CI comment commit, etc.) to compare against the PR's current head.

tools.name: ci_list_runs
tools.description: Prefer this over `gh run list` or `mcp__github__actions_list` (can silently drop filters). List recent CI runs, filtered.

workflow.description: Workflow filename, display name, or numeric ID

groupBy.description: Runner-minutes mode: self-hosted vs GitHub-hosted job minutes over `created` (required), grouped by this.

tools.name: ci_rerun
tools.description: Prefer this over `gh run rerun` via shell. Rerun failed jobs, a specific job, the whole run, or up to 50 runs in one batch call. scope: "failed" (default) reruns only failed jobs, auto-escalating to a full run rerun when a job was left `cancelled` by an upstream dependency failure — GitHub's rerun-failed-jobs endpoint never reschedules those (LS-9212); check the response `scope`/`message` for `"run (escalated from failed-jobs)"`. scope: "job" reruns a single job via jobId or jobName (single-run only; see jobName param). scope: "all" reruns the entire run. Pass runIds (1-50) instead of runId to rerun several runs independently in one call — scope "job" and withDiagnostics are single-run only; batch results use the standard partial-failure shape { success, total, succeeded, failed }. withDiagnostics: true (single-run, scope "failed" only) is the triage-then-rerun one-shot: fetches a short failure-log snippet and richer per-job payload before rerunning, and errors clearly (never a silent no-op) when there are no failed jobs to rerun.

runId.description: Run ID (single-run mode). Exactly one of runId/runIds is required.

runIds.description: Run IDs to rerun independently (1-50, batch mode). Not with runId, scope="job", or withDiagnostics.

scope.description: What to rerun: "failed" (default), "job" (needs jobId/jobName, single-run only), or "all".

jobId.description: Job ID to rerun; scope="job", single-run only.

jobName.description: jobId alternative for scope="job": case-insensitive substring match against the run's job list; errors on zero or multiple matches.

withDiagnostics.description: Single-run, scope="failed" only. Fetch a failure-log snippet and richer per-job payload before rerunning.

withFreshLogs.description: withDiagnostics only. Include a follow-up hint pointing at the ci_get_logs call for fresh failure logs once the new attempt completes.

tools.name: ci_retry_runner_flake
tools.description: Single-call detect-and-retry for the recurring self-hosted-runner-shutdown flake: given a PR number, checks whether the repo's own "CI: Runner Flake" label and "runner shutdown" bot comment are present (applied by ci-orchestrator.yml when a self-hosted runner shuts down mid-run), and if so, extracts the run ID and reruns the affected failed job(s) via the same path as ci_rerun({ withDiagnostics: true }) — without the caller first grepping logs to confirm the failure signature. When both are absent, falls back (LS-9334) to scanning the most recent run's failed/cancelled job logs for the shutdown signature first. Returns a clear, non-error result (never a false positive on a genuine failure) when no signal is found, pointing at ci_rerun({ runId, withDiagnostics: true }) as the manual fallback. Kept separate from ci_rerun: its prNumber input and shutdown-detection precondition give it a materially different schema — the documented escape hatch in the consolidation standard.

prNumber.description: PR number to check for the runner-shutdown flake signal and retry if detected.

tools.name: ci_search_logs
tools.description: Prefer this over `gh run view --log | grep` via shell. Search CI logs by pattern with optional regex and context lines.

runId.description: Run ID (required when jobId is not provided)

pattern.description: Search string or regex pattern. Note: `|` alone does NOT enable alternation (a|b|c) — it is matched as a literal pipe character unless isRegex is also set to true.

failedOnly.description: Failed steps only (default: true). WARNING: when the job whose logs contain the searched-for text actually succeeded, this can silently exclude it from the search entirely — the response will still return totalMatches: 0, but with a scopeNote explaining 0 jobs were searched. Set false to search all jobs regardless of conclusion.

truncateLineLength.description: Truncate every line (the matched line and every before/after context line) longer than this many characters. Defaults to 500 for the matched line and 200 for context lines when omitted.

maxChars.description: Hard cap on total output characters (default: 50000). Prevents context overflow when limitMatches and context lines together still produce a large response — trailing matches are dropped until the response fits.

tools.name: ci_session_stats
tools.description: Summarise tool-use counts and message metrics for a Claude Code session transcript. Returns total messages, first/last timestamp, per-tool call counts, and bashFallbackRatio (Bash count / total tool uses) — a quick "how MCP-first was this session?" heuristic. Optionally aggregates subagent transcripts into the totals and breaks them out per-subagent. Defaults to the most recently modified parent JSONL when sessionId is omitted.

sessionId.description: Parent session UUID. Defaults to the most recently modified parent JSONL.

project.description: Project slug (e.g. "D--code-legacy-sports"). Auto-detected from CWD if omitted.

lineRange.description: Only count messages in this 1-based [start, end] line range — useful for analysing a specific phase of a long session.

includeSubagents.description: Aggregate subagent stats into the parent totals and return per-subagent breakdowns (default: false).

tools.name: ci_unwedge_orchestrator
tools.description: Prefer this over the raw `gh run list`/`gh api .../jobs`/`gh run view` cancel+ci:run-label sequence. Detects and recovers a wedged ci-orchestrator.yml run: stuck `pending` with 0 jobs, holding the `orchestrator-<PR#>` concurrency group so CI Gate never posts (LS-7752). Finds the PR's stalest pending 0-job run older than staleAfterSeconds (default 300s), cancels it, polls for confirmed cancellation, then applies the "ci:run" label to redispatch via workflow_dispatch. Bounded ~12s per call — an unconfirmed cancellation returns { status: "cancelling", runId, hint } (never an error); re-invoke with that runId to resume without re-discovering/re-cancelling. Other outcomes: "clean" (no wedge found), "unnecessary" (run finished on its own, not wedged), "redispatched" (recovered).

prNumber.description: PR number whose ci-orchestrator.yml run may be wedged.

runId.description: Resume mode: runId from a prior { status: "cancelling" } response. Skips discovery/re-cancellation.

staleAfterSeconds.description: Min age (s) before a pending 0-job run counts as wedged. Default 300.

maxWaitSeconds.description: Max wait for cancellation confirmation per call (default/cap: 12s).

tools.name: ci_view_run
tools.description: Prefer this over `gh run view` via shell. View a CI run summary with jobs and conclusions. Pass runIds (1-50) instead of runId to inspect several runs independently in one call (e.g. checking CI across multiple PRs before merging) — attempt and format are single-run only; batch results use the standard partial-failure shape { success, total, succeeded, failed }.

runId.description: Run ID (single-run mode). Exactly one of runId/runIds is required.

runIds.description: Run IDs to inspect independently (1-50, batch mode). Not with runId or attempt.

format.description: Output format for single-run mode. "markdown" (default) returns a compact summary with a job table and a Failed Jobs section. "json" returns the full structured payload. Batch mode always returns structured JSON per run.

tools.name: ci_view_run_jobs
tools.description: Prefer this over `gh run view --json jobs` via shell. List per-job name, status, and conclusion for a specific CI run. Use this to confirm all jobs passed before merging a PR. Returns a summary (total, passed, failed, skipped, inProgress, allPassed) plus per-job details. Use filter to narrow to a specific conclusion (e.g. "failure" to see only failed jobs). This is complementary to ci_view_run (run-level summary) and ci_get_logs (log output for failed jobs).

filter.description: Filter jobs by conclusion ("failure"/"success"/"skipped"/"cancelled"), or by status for jobs with no conclusion yet ("in_progress" for currently running jobs, "queued"/"pending" for jobs still waiting on a runner — e.g. finding a wedged job directly instead of eyeballing a full job dump). Omit to return all jobs.

includeSteps.description: Include per-step breakdown for each job (default: false)

tools.name: ci_wait_run
tools.description: Wait for a workflow run to complete, bounded at 20s per call (stays under this Lambda-hosted server's own 30s execution timeout). Returns { status: "completed", conclusion } when the run finishes, or a { status: "in_progress", hint } snapshot (never an error) if it has not — re-invoke to continue waiting. Use after ci_dispatch_workflow returns in_progress, or after a session resume to re-attach to a run without re-dispatching.

maxWaitSeconds.description: Max wait per call in seconds (default and cap: 20)

tools.name: ci_workflow_info
tools.description: List workflows or get details for a specific workflow. Optionally includes App installation permissions.

workflow.description: Workflow filename or numeric ID; omit to list all

includePermissions.description: Include GitHub App installation permissions (default: false)

tools.name: ci_workflow_set_state
tools.description: Enable or disable a GitHub Actions workflow. Wraps `gh workflow enable/disable <workflow>` via the REST API. Returns the workflow state after the change. Use "enable" to restore a disabled workflow, "disable" to halt automatic runs (e.g. during incident recovery). To read state without modifying it, use ci_workflow_info with a specific workflow.

action.description: "enable" restores a disabled workflow; "disable" halts automatic runs

servers.label: GitHub
servers.summary: Pull request and review lifecycle — PR dashboards, review threads, labels, and merge readiness.

tools.name: get_job_logs
tools.description: Fetch GitHub Actions job logs with server-side truncation. When a step is marked failed, the log is scoped to that step (scopedToFailingStep + failingSteps) before tail/char limits apply; otherwise falls back to the whole log. Returns the last tail_lines lines (default 200), capped at max_chars (default 10 000). Use truncate_line_length to cap one long line, error_summary for error/failure lines only, or grep_pattern for a substring search. Provide job_id for a single job, or run_id for matching jobs (failed_only/conclusions/job_name_contains/list_only).

job_id.description: Specific job ID. Required when run_id is not provided.

run_id.description: Workflow run ID. Fetches logs for all jobs in the run (filtered by failed_only). Required when job_id is not provided.

failed_only.description: With run_id, keep non-success jobs (default true, incl. cancelled).

conclusions.description: Exact conclusions to keep, e.g. ["cancelled"]; supersedes failed_only.

list_only.description: Requires run_id. List matching jobs, no logs (see limit/offset).

tail_lines.description: Max lines from the end of the log (default 200).

tailLines.description: camelCase alias for tail_lines; tail_lines wins if both set.

max_chars.description: Hard cap on output characters (default: 10 000); truncated output is suffixed with the total byte count.

error_summary.description: Extract only error/failure lines (plus 2 lines of context) instead of tailing.

truncate_line_length.description: Truncate lines longer than this many characters (e.g. 500), so one pathologically long line can't alone consume the max_chars budget.

grep_pattern.description: Substring search (plus 2 lines context) instead of tailing. Case-insensitive; excl. error_summary.

failed_step_only.description: Force step-scoping; sets stepScopeFailed if no span is found, instead of a silent unscoped fallback.

tools.name: github_auth_status
tools.description: Check GitHub API authentication status (passive check only — does not trigger interactive auth). Call this first in any GitHub workflow to verify API access is available. Also see ci_auth_status for GitHub rate limit info.

tools.name: github_await_ref
tools.description: Bounded wait for a git ref to change SHA or be deleted — a transport-safe replacement for `git ls-remote | sleep` polling loops. Each call polls the ref for up to maxWaitSeconds (capped at 55s to survive the MCP transport timeout) and returns a { status: "changed" | "deleted" | "unchanged" } snapshot. On "unchanged", re-invoke with the same params (per the returned hint) to keep waiting — never an error while the condition is unmet.

ref.description: Ref to await, e.g. "refs/heads/main", "heads/main", or bare "main" (defaults to a branch ref).

changedFrom.description: Baseline SHA to diff against — waits until the ref SHA differs from this.

deleted.description: When true, waits for the ref to stop existing rather than to change SHA.

maxWaitSeconds.description: Per-call wait budget in seconds, capped at 55 (default 55).

tools.name: github_bulk_comment
tools.description: Batch variant of github_comment_pr. Post a top-level comment on many PRs in one call (1-50). For sweeping the same body across PRs, the same body can simply be supplied per item. Returns { success, total, succeeded, failed } per the shared batch-tool convention.

tools.name: github_bulk_edit
tools.description: Batch variant of github_edit_pr. Update title and/or body across many PRs in one call (1-50). For label changes across many PRs use github_manage_labels (it already accepts an array of PR numbers). Each item is { number, title?, body? } — at least one of title/body required per item. Returns { success, total, succeeded, failed } per the shared batch-tool convention.

items.description: PR edits (1-50). Each entry needs at least title or body.

tools.name: github_bulk_merge
tools.description: Batch variant of github_merge_pr. Merge many PRs in one call (1-50). Each item is { number, strategy? } where strategy defaults to "queue" (auto-merge via GraphQL) and "direct" uses admin REST merge. Returns { success, total, succeeded, failed } per the shared batch-tool convention — one PR's failure does not abort the rest.

strategy.description: "queue" (default) enables auto-merge; "direct" merges via admin REST.

tools.name: github_bulk_rebase
tools.description: Rebase many PR branches onto base and force-push (1-50). Runs sequentially because rebase mutates the local checkout. Returns { success, total, succeeded, failed } per the shared batch-tool convention — one PR's rebase conflict does not abort the rest. Conflict details are captured in the per-PR error. Budgeted to ~45s of synchronous work: larger batches return { jobId, status: "running" } — poll with github_job_wait (per-PR progress in logTail) until it returns the final batch result. Do NOT re-run the command while the job is in progress.

prs.description: PR numbers to rebase (1-50). Processed in order. Alias: "numbers".

tools.name: github_bulk_reply_to_review
tools.description: Batch variant of github_reply_to_review. Post replies on many review threads in one call (1-50). Each reply takes EITHER threadId (GraphQL node ID) OR commentId + number/prNumber (REST) — the same resolution rules as the single-item tool, mixed within one batch. Returns { success, total, succeeded, failed } per the shared batch-tool convention. For the structured Author Agent end-of-round flow (FIX/JUSTIFY/CANNOT-COMPLY with auto-resolve), prefer github_finish_fix_round.

threadId.description: GraphQL node ID of the review thread (use this OR commentId+number, not both).

commentId.description: Numeric REST comment databaseId. Requires number/prNumber.

number.description: PR number — required when using commentId. Alias: prNumber.

prNumber.description: Alias for "number".

tools.name: github_close_pr
tools.description: Close a PR with optional comment. Pass the PR number as "number" (preferred) or "prNumber" (alias).

prNumber.description: Alias for "number" — use either, not both

tools.name: github_comment_pr
tools.description: Post a general (top-level) comment on a PR. Use for diagnostic notes, blocker explanations, and status updates — distinct from review thread replies (use github_reply_to_review for those). Maps to POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}/comments. Pass the PR number as "number" (preferred) or "prNumber" (alias).

prNumber.description: Alias for "number" — use either, not both

tools.name: github_create_label
tools.description: Create a label; upserts if it exists. Description capped at 100 chars.

tools.name: github_edit_pr
tools.description: Update a PR's title and/or body. Use when Copilot or reviewers request description fixes. Maps to PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}. Pass the PR number as "number" (preferred) or "prNumber" (alias).

prNumber.description: Alias for "number" — use either, not both

bodyFile.description: Repo-relative file path replacing PR body (contents become public); exclusive with body, no Lambda support

tools.name: github_ensure_sweep_labels
tools.description: Idempotently ensure the sweep coordination labels (sweep-claimed, sweep-stale-claim) exist on the repository. Safe to call at sweep startup every time — creates missing labels and no-ops if they already exist.

tools.name: github_finish_fix_round
tools.description: Semantic one-shot for the Author Agent Contract end-of-round: posts per-thread FIX/JUSTIFY/CANNOT-COMPLY replies, resolves the FIX threads, and applies bot:ready-for-review to re-trigger the Reviewer Bot. Replaces github_reply_to_review_thread → github_resolve_threads → github_manage_labels. Every reply is validated before any side effect, so one invalid entry rejects the whole call; after that, a failed reply lands in `errors[]` and leaves its thread unresolved without blocking the rest. Only FIX threads are resolved. Use issueId (not threadId) for a PR-level finding with no file/line. Reply format and the full contract: .agents/skills/pr-lifecycle/references/respond-to-review.md.

prNumber.description: PR number

number.description: Alias for "prNumber" — use either, not both

threadId.description: GraphQL thread node ID (PRRT_...) for an inline (file+line) finding. Exactly one of threadId/issueId is required.

issueId.description: Issue-id (ULID) of a PR-level (threadless — no file/line) finding, from the `<!-- issue-id: ... -->` marker in the bot review body. Posts a top-level PR comment instead of a thread reply. Exactly one of threadId/issueId is required.

kind.description: Reply kind per Author Agent Contract

sha.description: Commit SHA the fix is committed at. Required when kind=FIX; ignored otherwise.

body.description: Rationale text. Required when kind=JUSTIFY or CANNOT-COMPLY; ignored for FIX.

replies.description: One entry per thread. Omit or [] for a label-only re-trigger.

readyLabel.description: Label to apply after replying + resolving (default: bot:ready-for-review)

tools.name: github_get_branch_protection
tools.description: Read branch protection rules and GitHub rulesets for a branch. Returns required status checks (from both classic protection and active rulesets), conversation resolution requirement, required review count, whether a code-owner review is required (requireCodeOwnerReview — note this can be true while requiredReviewCount is 0), and a summary of all rulesets.
